source.title: Do Small Language Models Learn to Negotiate? A Controlled Scaling Study of RL-Trained Sellers

record.tranche_reason: It tests how downstream negotiation performance varies across language-model sizes, using task scores rather than held-out cross-entropy loss or a fitted scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no held-out pretraining-loss measurements, power-law fits, extrapolations, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its relevant results are downstream negotiation scores across Gemma 4 sizes and training settings. Deal rate, welfare, formatting, and buyer-specific diagnostics are not separately cataloged as scaling results; they are task diagnostics rather than measures of a fitted downstream scaling relationship.
record.test_reason: It reports negotiation scores for four Gemma 4 sizes (2.3B–31B) as base and GRPO-trained sellers. This bears on V6 (downstream performance improving with scale) in a new setting: multi-turn negotiation after RL. It measures no pretraining loss, fits no law and does no allocation, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. T3 fits better than T2 because the novelty is the setting, not a new method on the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add three points: base models' point estimates already rank by size; the 3× LR improves on the shared rate at every size at early checkpoints; and the 10× LR arm's gain concentrates on the same-family buyer. The authors explicitly fit no scaling law, citing single runs and confounding of size with architecture and FLOPs.
record.recipe_differences: The original claim concerns held-out pretraining cross-entropy scaling and compute-optimal allocation. This study instead trains Gemma 4 sellers with GRPO and evaluates programmatic negotiation utility across sizes; it does not fit a loss law or optimize a fixed-compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes scores and RL gains; the held-out domain changes the apparent size/gain ordering. Architecture changes between the 4.5B E-series and 12B conventional checkpoint, and training FLOPs increase with size at matched steps.

fits_no_version.finding: The RL (GRPO) gain over base grows with model size under a shared learning rate: +0.001 (n.s.) at 2.3B, +0.023 at 4.5B, +0.063 at 12B, +0.078 at 31B. Tripling the learning rate changes this pattern, with the largest gain at 4.5B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gains from RL post-training on agentic tasks grow with base-model size, depending on learning rate.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026), Workshop: SLMs for Agentic Systems
record.problems: Four sizes from one model family; one training run per size-by-rate arm; architecture and parameter count co-vary; arms are matched on steps rather than FLOPs; learning rates are not tuned per size; held-out-domain evaluation has n = 128. The reported bootstrap intervals capture scenario sampling, not run-to-run variance. No scaling law is fitted.
record.rows_left_out: No Gemma score rows from Table 4 were omitted. Other negotiation metrics and diagnostic analyses were not included as separate scaling rows because the cataloged measure is the primary seller score S; the paper does not report those diagnostics as fitted scaling relationships.

untested.parts: No shape-at-fixed-size comparison; architecture is confounded with size.
Not tested. RL post-training gain scaling is recorded under fits_no_version instead.
No fitted exponents and no comparison of fitting choices.

Untested: whether improvement is predictable (no functional fit, one run per size, no extrapolation); any relation to pretraining loss; and separation of size from architecture and FLOPs (E-series vs conventional checkpoints).

missing.what: Paired cross-size contrast of attained scores: 12B vs 31B 3× LR difference is +0.021 [+0.003, +0.040], barely excluding zero and confounded by read point.

record.verdict_notes: Dropped the reader's third limits_scope label. The absence of a fitted law and the size/architecture/FLOP confounding are untested parts of V6 or design caveats, not results showing V6 failing. Only four sizes from one family, one run each; intervals reflect scenario sampling only. Pooled ordering holds across RL arms, but the RL arms receive more FLOPs at larger sizes (matched steps).

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss or power-law relationship in parameters, tokens, or compute is measured.
No small-run fit or prediction of much larger runs is performed.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token split is studied.
Architecture varies with size, but the study does not isolate architecture effects on loss.
No other modality or the listed repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws are tested.

The study measures negotiation-task scores across four sizes and several training settings, but does not test a general predictive law, relate downstream performance to pretraining loss, or extrapolate to untested sizes.
Learning rate and architecture affect the reported task results, but the study does not compare fitted scaling exponents, compute-optimal splits, or alternative loss-curve fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Pooled over all nine domains: base sellers and both GRPO learning-rate series
relationships.reason: Score point estimates rise monotonically with size in base (R01–R04), shared-LR 104-step (R06, R08, R10, R13) and 3× LR (R14, R15, R17, R18) series. The 2.3B-to-4.5B base step is tiny.
relationships.display_finding: Pooled score estimates increased monotonically with size in all three series, although the base-model gain from 2.3B to 4.5B was tiny.

relationships.reason: 4.5B scores below 2.3B in base (R19 vs R20), shared-LR (R23–R26) and 3× LR (R32–R34) arms. The authors say the full ordering does not replicate; estimates are imprecise.
relationships.display_finding: The 4.5B model scored below 2.3B under base, shared-learning-rate and tripled-learning-rate settings across 128 evaluations, although estimates were imprecise.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Base sellers and headline shared-LR and 3×-LR checkpoints, pooled over all nine evaluation domains
reader_labels.reason: Point estimates of S increase with size in the base series (R01–R04), the shared-LR 104-step series (R06, R08, R10, R13), and the 3×-LR step-56 series (R14, R15, R17, R18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The smallest sizes do not maintain the pooled ordering: the 4.5B held-out score is below the 2.3B score in the base and 3×-LR comparisons, and the paper says the full gain ordering does not replicate there; estimates use only 128 episodes and are imprecise (R19–R20, R25–R26, R32–R34).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the tested Gemma 4 size comparisons
reader_labels.reason: The authors fit no scaling law, trained each size only once, and state that size co-varies with architecture and training FLOPs, so the observed task-score ordering is not an isolated or validated predictive size law (R01–R18).
